summary: This article explains what veterinarians do, how they find out what is wrong with animals that cannot talk, how animal hospitals and vaccines keep animals and people healthy, and how everyone can help.
introduce: Show the title “Animal Hospitals and Vets” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a doctor trained to care for animals
to find out what illness or problem someone has
a tool doctors use to listen to the heart and lungs

challengeTerms.def: signs that show someone may be sick, such as fever or pain
an operation in which a doctor repairs something inside the body
a medicine, often a shot, that helps the body fight a sickness before it starts

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that being a vet is harder than being a doctor for people? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a vet figures out what is wrong with an animal that cannot talk.
struggling: Pre-teach veterinarian, diagnose, and stethoscope with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses symptoms, surgery, and vaccine to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
